AXP.rationale: American Express demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating revenue growth (+11% YoY in Q1 2026), robust EPS growth (+18% YoY to $4.28), and exceptional ROE of 35%. The company's closed-loop, spend-centric model targeting affluent consumers provides durable competitive advantages and pricing power. Quarterly trajectory shows consistent improvement: revenue grew from $9.63B to $10.52B over four quarters, with EPS rising from $3.64 to $4.28. Valuation is attractive versus its own history—current P/E of 19.75 sits near the bottom of its 18.3-25.3 range over the past year, and P/B of 6.52 is also near the low end of 6.0-8.2. The stock has pulled back ~10% in the latest quarter despite strong fundamentals, creating a potential entry point. Credit metrics remain pristine with net write-off rate at 2.3% and delinquencies at 1.3%. Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance of 9-10% revenue growth and EPS of $17.30-$17.90 while increasing investments in marketing and technology. Near-term catalysts include continued momentum in Millennial/Gen-Z card acquisitions (largest and fastest-growing cohort) and potential benefit from easing macro conditions. Risks include elevated oil prices potentially impacting consumer spending and geopolitical uncertainties, though Amex's affluent customer base provides relative insulation. The combination of strong execution, attractive valuation versus history, and a credible near-term earnings trajectory supports a mildly-to-moderately positive view.
